caption:
How Laser Tattoo Removal Works
- Laser tattoo removal uses powerful pulses of light to break tattoo ink into tiny fragments beneath the skin. Over the following weeks, immune cells help clear these particles through the lymphatic system, gradually fading the tattoo with each session.
on_screen_hook: This is what a laser does to a tattoo. Take a look
transcript: This is what a laser does to a tattoo. Take a look at the ink. It sits below the surface in the dermis, held inside immune cells that cannot break it down. The laser fires a pulse lasting only billions of a second. The ink absorbs the light, heats faster than it can cool, and shatters into fragments. The white frosting is gas released in that instant. Now the pieces are small enough to move. Over the following weeks, immune cells carry them away through the lymphatic system. Session by session, weeks apart, the color fades until only skin remains.

transcript: I want to preface this by saying that this does not mean that you had a bad Botox job. It certainly can be due to injection technique, but every single experienced injector in the best in the world have had several eyelid ptosis and any injector that tells you otherwise is either lying or a brand new injector. However, what does really matter when going to an injector is not to ensure that they've never had any complications occur before because that's actually not a good sign. You want an injector with that kind of experience and knowledge of how to treat those complications if and when they occur, but you want to ensure that your injector is being upfront and transparent on the front end about the risk of complications, what that would look like when you start to see these complications occur and how they would manage them. An eyelid ptosis occurs because neurotoxin diffuses into this levator palpebrae superioris muscle that works to keep the lid open. We know that neurotoxin is an opposite drug, meaning it makes the muscle do the opposite of what it naturally does. So if that muscle naturally keeps the lid open, it makes sense that toxin would do the opposite and try to close that lid, also causing the unaffected eye to work harder and overcompensate and recruit. Now for this muscle that can't work as hard, which is why her other eye, the unaffected side, appears to be bulging or bug eye. And this can happen due to extrusion force, so how quickly the volume in the syringe is being pushed, also the direction of the needle. It typically happens when we're injecting the lateral corrugators. Depth matters if we're too deep, if the needle is directed towards that frame in. So also lying down flat within four hours, exercising within 24 hours, and massaging or manipulating the injection site within four weeks of a tox treatment before it has had a chance to fully settle can all increase the risk of acquiring an eyelid ptosis. So I treated this patient by injecting two units originally in the pre-torsal muscle here. So the pre-torsal muscle is one of the muscles that works to close the lid, meaning it will have the opposite effect and help to open the lid. title: Hair transformation with PRP!
caption:
Witness the incredible transformation of PRP! 

PRP (Platelet-Rich Plasma) is a three- step medical treatment in which a person’s blood is drawn, processed and separated and then injected into the areas of the scalp which need increased hair growth. Patients typically do a series of 3 treatments spaced 4 weeks apart. 

PRP uses the plasma from your blood which contains special proteins and growth factors that help reduce inflammation and help repair the hair follicle to stimulate hair growth. PR
